title: Topic 5 Climate change - Hodder practice questions

questions.question_text: Figure 5.14 shows annual global surface temperature change for land and ocean, compared to the 1901-2000 average. Estimate the largest negative temperature difference from the twentieth-century average.
Estimate the largest positive temperature difference from the twentieth-century average.
Identify the decades when temperatures were lowest.
Identify the decade when temperatures were highest.
Estimate the increase in temperature between the decades with the lowest temperatures and the decade with the highest temperatures.

points: 1 mark for showing working/values, 1 mark for correct final answer of 1.4°C [1]
marking_scheme.rubric: Award up to 2 marks: 1.4°C (accept 1.3–1.5°C). 1 mark for correct method/reading, 1 mark for accurate answer.

questions.question_text: Distinguish between the greenhouse effect and global warming.

points: The greenhouse effect is a natural process where greenhouse gases (water vapour, CO₂, CH₄) in the atmosphere trap outgoing long-wave infrared radiation [1], keeping the Earth warm enough to support life (c. +15°C average) [1]

Global warming is the gradual increase in average global surface temperatures caused primarily by human activities (burning fossil fuels, deforestation) [1] which increase atmospheric concentrations of greenhouse gases, enhancing the natural greenhouse effect [1]
marking_scheme.rubric: Award up to 4 marks. 2 marks for explaining the natural greenhouse effect, and 2 marks for explaining human-induced global warming.

questions.question_text: Define climate change mitigation and climate change adaptation.

points: Mitigation: Strategies and actions aimed at reducing or preventing the emission of greenhouse gases, or enhancing carbon sinks, to tackle the root cause of climate change (e.g. renewable energy, afforestation) [1]

Adaptation: Actions taken to adjust to the actual or expected impacts and consequences of climate change to reduce vulnerability and harm (e.g. building sea walls, planting drought-resistant crops) [1]
marking_scheme.rubric: Award 1 mark for definition of mitigation and 1 mark for definition of adaptation.

questions.question_text: Evaluate techniques of climate change mitigation and adaptation.

inputs.label: Nhập bài làm Case Study (7 marks):

points: Mitigation techniques: Transition to renewable energy (solar, wind, HEP); carbon capture and storage (CCS); afforestation and reforestation; international agreements (Paris Accord, COP targets); carbon taxes [2-3 marks]

Adaptation techniques: Coastal defenses (sea walls, mangrove restoration); water management (drip irrigation, rainwater harvesting); agricultural adjustments (flood/drought-resistant seeds); climate-resilient building design (elevated homes on stilts in Bangladesh) [2-3 marks]

Evaluation / Case Study: Contrast costs, feasibility, and timeframes. Mitigation addresses the long-term cause but requires global cooperation and massive capital; adaptation is immediately necessary for vulnerable communities (e.g. Bangladesh, Tuvalu) but does not stop warming. Both must be implemented concurrently [1-2 marks]
marking_scheme.rubric: Level 1 (1-3 marks): Simple descriptions of methods to fight climate change without distinguishing clearly between mitigation and adaptation. Level 2 (4-6 marks): Explains specific mitigation and adaptation techniques with case study examples and some discussion of effectiveness. Level 3 (7 marks): Comprehensive evaluation comparing the strengths and limitations of both mitigation and adaptation, supported by named examples, concluding that both are vital and interdependent.
